meta.title: Ask Sahayak
meta.description: Ask about intellectual property or regulation for an Ayurvedic product.

heading: Sahayak
standfirst: Ask about intellectual property or regulation for an Ayurvedic product. Answers are built from cited sources.
demoNotice: No documents have been ingested yet, so this was answered from a small set of demonstration sources. What happened is real — the search, the sources chosen, the confidence and its reason. The text behind each source is a placeholder until the documents themselves are fetched.
emptyBody: Type a question on the homepage, or use the example below.

composer.label: Your question
composer.placeholder: Ask about protecting, registering, manufacturing or selling an Ayurvedic product…
composer.detectionNote: Detected from the script you typed in. Correct it if it is wrong.
composer.shortcutHint: Ctrl+K to focus, Ctrl+Enter to send, / for examples

items.reformulated: We reformulated a classical preparation — is there anything patentable in it?
items.manufacturing: What do we need in place before manufacturing an Ayurvedic product in India?
items.uk: How do we file one international patent application for several countries?
items.brandName: Can we register our brand name if it contains a classical formulation name?
items.gi: Does our regional herb qualify for a geographical indication?
items.healthClaim: How is an Ayurveda Aahara food product regulated, and where do we apply?
items.classification: Is our product a medicine, a nutraceutical or a cosmetic?
items.wildCollect: We wild-collect a herb — what compliance applies before we commercialise?
items.bioSource: Do we need to declare the biological source in a patent application?
items.multiCountry: How do we protect the brand in several countries at once?

status.routedElsewhere: You asked about “{{marker}}”, so this was answered from {{jurisdiction}} sources rather than the jurisdiction selected above.

nothing_relevant.title: I couldn't find anything in these sources that answers this reliably
nothing_relevant.body: Try narrowing the jurisdiction, naming the product type, or rephrasing. You can also see what's covered, or send this to a human IP facilitator with the context already filled in.

out_of_scope.title: This is outside what I can answer
out_of_scope.body: I cover intellectual property and regulatory requirements for Ayurvedic products — not clinical advice, individual legal opinions, or predictions about whether an application will succeed.

sources_conflict.title: The only passages I found point different ways
sources_conflict.body: Rather than pick one, here are both, with the documents they came from. Which governs is the question to put to someone qualified.

sources_out_of_date.title: What I found sits outside its effective window
sources_out_of_date.body: The position on record here may have changed. The passages and their dates are below.

needs_more_facts.title: This turns on something only you can tell me
needs_more_facts.body: What your product is regulatorily decides the answer, and answering for every possibility would be worse than asking.

language_unsupported.title: This question could not be searched
language_unsupported.body: The sources are in English and no translation service is configured, so this question was never put into a language they could be searched in. Nothing was found because nothing was looked for — not because the sources are silent.

error.title: The answer could not be produced
error.unreachable: The service could not be reached. Check that it is running, then try again. Nothing has been answered.
error.offline: This device is not connected, so nothing was searched. Reconnect and try again — your question is still in the box.
error.generation_unavailable: Sources were found, but nothing is configured to write an answer from them. Nothing has been answered.
error.rate_limited: Too many questions in a short time. Wait a moment, then try again.
error.request_too_large: That question was too large to send. Shorten it and try again.
error.question_too_long: That question is longer than this accepts. Shorten it and try again.
error.unknown: Something went wrong on the way to an answer. Nothing has been answered, and nothing was guessed.
error.timeout: The search took too long and was stopped. Nothing has been answered. A shorter question usually finishes.

records.note: Filed or granted records. Evidence of what was filed, not a statement of law, and never part of the answer above.
records.empty: No related records for this question.
records.stillAbstained: These records do not answer the question. The system still declined, and they are shown only because they exist.

elsewhere.heading: This product did not search these
elsewhere.notSearched: These registries are interactive, and their terms generally do not allow a product like this one to search them automatically. So it has not. What follows is where to look yourself, not a set of places that have been checked — finding nothing here would mean nothing.
elsewhere.linkPending: Link not yet verified, so none is offered. Search this registry directly.
elsewhere.none: No registries are listed for this.

escalate.title: Send this to a human
escalate.intro: This packages what you asked and what the system found into a summary you can copy or send. There is no expert network behind this button — it is an honest handoff, not a queue.
escalate.channels: Official facilitation channels are listed on the sources page.

flows.offerHeading: This depends on something the answer does not know

classify.offer: This depends on what your product is regulatorily. Work it out — a few questions.
classify.title: What is your product, regulatorily?
classify.intro: The fewest questions that settle it. Anything already known is skipped, and you can change any answer afterwards.
classify.singleClass: On these answers, this is a {{class}}.
classify.multipleClasses: On these answers, more than one route may be open.
classify.consequencesNote: A general orientation. Ask Sahayak for the cited detail on your own product.
classify.apply: Use this as my product type

questions.external_use: Is it applied externally for appearance rather than for a therapeutic effect?
questions.food_route: Is it intended as a food or a supplement rather than as a medicine?
questions.therapeutic_claim: Are you making a specific therapeutic claim for it?
questions.purified_fraction: Is any ingredient a purified or standardised extract or fraction, rather than a whole-plant preparation?
questions.classical_unmodified: Is the formulation, and the method of making it, taken from an authoritative classical text unmodified?
questions.novel_ingredient: Does it contain a non-Ayurvedic or otherwise novel ingredient?
questions.human_evidence: Do you have human evidence of its safety and effectiveness?
questions.changed_formulation: Have you changed the ingredients, the proportions, the dosage form or the method?

changes.cosmetic: Making a therapeutic claim for it would take this out of the cosmetic route entirely.
changes.ayurveda_aahar: Making a specific therapeutic claim would move this towards a medicine, with a different regulator and different limits on what you may say.
changes.food_or_drug: Dropping the therapeutic claim would settle this as a food. Keeping it points at a medicine. The claim is the fork, and it is yours to choose.
changes.phytopharmaceutical: Using the whole-plant preparation rather than a purified or standardised fraction would move this back towards the classical or proprietary routes.
changes.classical_generic: Changing an ingredient, a proportion, the dosage form or the method would move this to the proprietary route — and with it, what you can protect.
changes.patent_proprietary: Returning to the text unmodified would move this back to the classical route. Adding a novel ingredient would move it on towards a new drug.
changes.new_non_classical_drug: Removing the novel ingredient would move this back towards the proprietary route.
changes.new_non_classical_drug_no_evidence: Removing the novel ingredient would move this back towards the proprietary route. Note also that you said you do not yet hold human evidence, which this route generally expects.

abs.offer: This touches access and benefit sharing. Work out where you stand — five questions.
abs.title: Where do you stand on access and benefit sharing?
abs.intro: An orientation aid, not a determination. It points at which authority is likely involved and what usually comes first.
abs.patent: How it meets a patent application
abs.amended: The Biological Diversity Act was amended in 2023 and its rules remade in 2024, so check the current position against the published instrument.

questions.access: Are you accessing a biological resource, or knowledge associated with one?
questions.purpose: Is the use research, or commercial?
questions.ip: Do you intend to seek intellectual property over anything that comes of it?
questions.knowledge: Is the knowledge you are drawing on codified in published texts, or held by a community?

abs.noTrigger: On these answers, nothing you have described accesses a biological resource or associated knowledge, so the access and benefit-sharing duties are not engaged. That can change the moment a resource enters the picture.

priorArt.offer: You can see what is already on the record for something like this — as orientation, not as a search.
priorArt.open: See what is on the record
priorArt.title: What is already on the record?
priorArt.intro: Describe the formulation and this builds the search terms an examiner would start from, and links to the official databases to search.
priorArt.inputPlaceholder: Ingredients, dosage form, what it is for…
priorArt.termsNote: Generated from what you typed. Add Sanskrit and vernacular names, botanical names and classification codes when you search.
priorArt.noRecords: No patent records are held on this site. Search the official databases linked below.
priorArt.elsewhereNote: These databases cannot be searched from here. Nothing on this page has been searched on your behalf.
priorArt.tkdlBody: This product cannot search it. Access is restricted to patent offices under access agreements, and no amount of orientation here substitutes for what an examiner will see there. If prior art matters to a decision you are about to take, that is a question for a patent professional.
priorArt.banner: This is an orientation aid, not a novelty search. Finding nothing here does not mean an invention is new.

l0.label: No review needed
l0.body: The sources answer what you asked. The limits listed here still apply to every answer.

l1.label: Facts missing
l1.body: You can take this further yourself by supplying the facts listed below.

l2.label: Expert review advised
l2.body: Something here is genuinely uncertain — an issue came out weak, or a conflict needs a person to look at it.

l3.label: Expert review needed
l3.body: Part of this turns on applying a provision to your facts, which is a judgement this product must not make for you.

conflicts.heading: Overlaps and conflicts
conflicts.standfirst: Two obligations can both apply without contradicting each other. Where one genuinely governs the other, the rule that decides it is named.

explanation.conflictJurisdictional: Two legal systems ask different things of the same product. Neither overrides the other.
explanation.conflictScopeOverlap: Different legal questions about one product, which can all apply at once.
explanation.conflictAuthority: The same point stated at different levels of authority.
explanation.conflictTemporalLater: The two took effect on different dates.
explanation.conflictClassification: More than one category is open on the facts given.
explanation.conflictMissingFact: A fact nobody has stated decides between two readings.
explanation.conflictTrueSource: Equal authority, same system, both in force, and still in tension.

protection.heading: What you could protect
protection.standfirst: Six kinds of protection, and where each stands on the facts you have given. “Needs more information” is not the same as “not available”.

reason.protectionProcessDescribed: You described a process or a distinctive feature.
reason.protectionNeedProcess: Nothing yet says whether there is a new process or technique.
reason.protectionPatentGeneral: A patent may be available for a new technical contribution.
reason.protectionNeedBrand: Nothing yet says whether a name or logo is involved.
reason.protectionNoBrand: No name or logo was mentioned.
reason.protectionNeedAppearance: Nothing yet describes the product's appearance or packaging.
reason.protectionLabelAndText: Label artwork, text and photographs are original work.
reason.protectionRegionMentioned: You mentioned a place of origin.
reason.protectionNoOriginClaim: No claim was made linking the product to a place.
reason.protectionKeptConfidential: You said it has been kept confidential.
reason.protectionAlreadyPublic: It has already been made public.
reason.protectionNeedDisclosure: Nothing yet says whether it has been kept confidential.

step.protectionStepPriorArtSearch: Run a prior-art search before filing anything.
step.protectionStepSearchRegister: Search the trade marks register for the name.
step.protectionStepDecideName: Decide whether you will sell under a name of your own.
step.protectionStepDesignNovelty: Check whether the appearance is new before you publish it.
step.protectionStepDescribeAppearance: Describe the shape, surface or packaging.
step.protectionStepKeepRecords: Keep dated records of who made the artwork and text.
step.protectionStepCheckGiRegister: Check whether a geographical indication already covers this.
step.protectionStepWriteItDown: Write down what is confidential and who has access.
step.protectionStepDecideDisclosure: Decide what has already been shown outside the company.
